title: Teams sign-in fails for lots of people in Silesia
scenario: A long case in which the customer first believes that all sites are affected and that a policy was changed, which is later corrected; the engineer tries two policy detours before the per-site pattern points to one DNS resolver, and a static setting on two laptops brings the problem back.

events.title: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text:
Hello, Teams sign-in fails for a lot of people since yesterday evening. I think all our sites are affected, around 200 people. The message is 'Teams cannot connect' with the code caa82ee7.

Dariusz Wrona | Network & Systems | Silesia Packaging Example
Please consider the environment before printing this e-mail.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Hello Dariusz, thank you. I need three names of affected people with a UTC moment for each, the sites without trouble and the sites with trouble, and a list of what was changed in identity, network, DNS or proxy configuration over the last two days.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Names and moments: w.kowal Mon 21:05 UTC, e.zajac Mon 21:40 UTC, b.sikora Tue 06:50 UTC. All sites fail as far as I know. Changes: on Monday at 16:00 UTC we changed the MFA rule in Conditional Access. Nothing in DNS or proxy that I am aware of.

events.title: Log search
events.text: Sign-in logs for w.kowal Mon 21:05, e.zajac Mon 21:40 and b.sikora Tue 06:50 UTC: none of the three attempts has a failed row.

events.title: Provider status
events.text: Provider status at 09:35 UTC: Teams and Entra ID show no open incident.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Our CIO says he read on social media that Microsoft has an outage today. I have not verified that.

events.title: Provider status, second look
events.text: Provider status, second look at 10:10 UTC: still no open incident for Teams and Entra ID.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Dariusz, thank you. As a first test, please exclude w.kowal, e.zajac and b.sikora from the MFA policy you changed on Monday, and tell me the time.

events.title: Teams does not sign in
events.text: Hi, I work in Gliwice and Teams will not let me in since last night, it shows caa82ee7.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: The three users were excluded at 10:40 UTC and still fail with caa82ee7.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Thank you. Next, please revoke the sessions of those same three users, let them log in again, and give me the time.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Sessions revoked at 12:05 UTC. The three tried again and failed again, no change.

events.title: Call from Dariusz Wrona
events.text: Call note, 13:30 UTC: Dariusz phoned, management is asking. He said the number is now about 260 people and that Zabrze 'seems fine', which he heard from the Zabrze manager and has not checked.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Dariusz, thank you for calling. Please send me a list of your sites with the number of people failing at each, and the DNS servers that each site receives by DHCP.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Katowice 150 people fail, Gliwice 110, Zabrze none. Katowice and Gliwice receive 10.60.0.2, 10.60.0.3 and 10.60.0.4 by DHCP, Zabrze receives 10.61.0.2 and 10.61.0.3.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Thanks. Katowice and Gliwice share three resolvers and Zabrze does not, so please let your network admin query statics.teams.cdn.office.net and login.microsoftonline.com on every one of those servers with Resolve-DnsName, from a Katowice machine. A reinstall of Teams is not needed for any of this.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: From a Katowice machine at 16:25 UTC. 10.60.0.2: both names answered. 10.60.0.3: both names answered. 10.60.0.4: login.microsoftonline.com answered, statics.teams.cdn.office.net returned NXDOMAIN in 5 of 10 queries.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: About the Conditional Access change I wrote about: I was wrong, that change was made in our test tenant, not in production. Sorry for the confusion.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: No problem, thank you for saying so. Please take 10.60.0.4 out of the DHCP scope of Katowice for now and tell me the time, and let somebody measure a sign-in request through every proxy node from Katowice to rule the proxy out.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: 10.60.0.4 was removed from the Katowice scope at 17:40 UTC. Proxy test from Katowice at 18:00 UTC: the three nodes answered within 0.7 s, five of five tries each.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Update 19:40 UTC: Katowice works for most people since about 17:50 UTC. Gliwice still has many people failing.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Thank you. Gliwice receives the same three servers, so please remove 10.60.0.4 from the Gliwice scope as well and tell me the time.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: 10.60.0.4 was removed from the Gliwice scope at 20:00 UTC.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Wednesday 07:40 UTC: Katowice and Gliwice both report no problems since last evening.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Good. Pulling the resolver out is a stop-gap. The lasting fix is to repair the filtering rule that makes it fail on the Microsoft CDN names: the rule needs an allowance for the endpoints Microsoft publishes for Microsoft 365, and the change should follow your usual change process. Please tell me when it is planned.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text:
The security team says the filtering vendor needs until Friday to correct the rule.

Dariusz Wrona | Network & Systems | Silesia Packaging Example
Please consider the environment before printing this e-mail.

events.title: Internal note
events.text: Internal note: stable on the workaround, next check on Friday after the vendor's change.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Wednesday 16:30 UTC: two people in Gliwice have the error again, caa82ee7.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Found it: both laptops have 10.60.0.4 typed in as a static DNS server, so they ignore DHCP. I set both to automatic at 17:10 UTC.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Both users sign in now.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Friday 10:00 UTC: the filtering vendor corrected the rule at 09:15 UTC and added an allowance for the Microsoft 365 hosts, and we put 10.60.0.4 back into the scopes at 09:45 UTC.

events.title: Re: Teams sign-in problem for lots of people
events.text: Comparison from Katowice at 10:30 UTC after the correction: all three servers answer both names in 10 of 10 queries each.

events.title: Numbers before and after
events.text: Teams sign-in tickets per day at the helpdesk: Tuesday 183, Wednesday 7, Thursday 0, and 0 on Friday until 11:00 UTC. At 10:55 UTC I let three sampled users sign in, and none of them got an error.

events.title: Resolution note
events.text: Resolution: workaround on Tuesday at 17:40 UTC (Katowice) and 20:00 UTC (Gliwice), permanent fix on Friday at 09:15 UTC; both are written up as separate items for the customer. Closing the case.

events.title: Closing summary
events.text: Dariusz, closing summary: the failures came from one resolver in the Katowice and Gliwice scopes. Workaround Tuesday, permanent fix Friday 09:15 UTC. Two laptops with a typed-in DNS server returned on Wednesday and were set to automatic. Should anything return, just answer on this case.
